An old gate in 大栅栏 has door gods whose colour has gone

explains.门神: 画在大门上的两个人，他们看门。

npcs.name: 瑞蚨祥的阿姨

wants: To see you in something that suits you

npcs.name: 内联升的师傅
npcs.role: the shoemaker at 内联升, stitching a sole at the counter
knows: 内联升 has made cloth shoes since the Qing dynasty
wants: To see you in something that suits you

nodes.translate: Hello! What would you like?
nodes.why: 戏园: 脸谱 30 元. Say what you want and how many — 「两个包子」, 「一瓶水」 — ask 「多少钱？」 any time, and say 「不要了」 when that is all.

nodes.speaker: hero
nodes.translate: So this is Qianmen!
nodes.why: 前门 — the Front Gate — stood at the south of the old inner city. 大栅栏, just east, is a lane of shops hundreds of years old.

nodes.translate: Hello! Do you like Beijing opera?

nodes.say: 你看这些脸谱。红脸是好人，白脸是坏人。
nodes.translate: Look at these masks. A red face is a good man, a white face a bad one.
nodes.why: In 京剧 the face paint tells you the character: red loyal and brave, white cunning, black honest and fierce.

nodes.translate: At the east end of 大栅栏 there's an old gate.

nodes.say: 门神的颜色都没了。你去看看吧。
nodes.translate: The door gods on it have lost all their colour. Go and have a look.

words.explain: 北京的老戏，有歌，有脸谱。

nodes.translate: Please sit, have some tea!

nodes.say: 那个门很老了。以前，门神很好看！
nodes.translate: That gate is very old. The door gods used to be beautiful!
nodes.why: 老 (old) is HSK 3 — a small key line. The door gods are on the gate right beside her.

nodes.speaker: menshen
nodes.translate: Hello, friend!

nodes.speaker: menshen
nodes.say: 我们的颜色都没了。你有红纸吗？
nodes.translate: Our colour is all gone. Have you got red paper?

nodes.speaker: menshen
nodes.translate: You've got red paper? Give it to us!

nodes.speaker: menshen
nodes.say: 你看，我们好看了！好看吗？
nodes.translate: Look — we're beautiful again! Aren't we?

nodes.speaker: menshen
nodes.say: 别画了！再画是画蛇添足。
nodes.translate: Stop painting! Any more would be 画蛇添足 — drawing feet on a snake.
nodes.why: A 成语 📌 with a story: a man who finished drawing his snake first added feet to it, and lost the prize. Adding more spoils it.

nodes.say: 你要看京剧吗？票五十块。
nodes.translate: Would you like to see the opera? Tickets are fifty.
Take a seat! …Wonderful, isn't it?
nodes.why: Gongs, a high voice, painted faces: 京剧 in a hundred-year-old theatre.

nodes.translate: All right, next time.

nodes.say: 我想喝老刘的茶叶。你能买吗？
nodes.translate: I miss 老刘's tea leaves. Could you get me some?
My tea! Thank you!

nodes.speaker: hero
nodes.translate: Right — one, two, three!

nodes.speaker: hero
nodes.translate: Right — one, two, three!
Come, taste the roast duck! I’ll show you. First take a pancake.
A little sauce.
Then the duck and the cucumber.
Roll it up and eat!
Delicious, eh? That’s Beijing roast duck!

words.explain: 一边到另一边，像一个小包。
水上的鸟，北京烤鸭就是它。

nodes.say: 京剧里，红脸是好人，白脸是坏人，黑脸不说假话。
nodes.translate: I’ll paint your face. The red face is a good man, the white face a bad one, the black face never lies.

nodes.say: 包公不说假话。他是红脸、白脸，还是黑脸？
nodes.translate: 包公 never lies. Which face is his?

nodes.say: 对！关公是好人。他是红脸、白脸，还是黑脸？
nodes.translate: Right! 关公 is a good, loyal man. And his?

nodes.say: 对了！你是京剧的朋友了！
nodes.translate: Right again! You’re a friend of the opera now!
nodes.why: 包公 was a famous honest judge; 关公, a general, stands for loyalty. The face tells the audience who someone is before he sings a note.

words.explain: 京剧里的红色的脸，是好人。
京剧里的白色的脸，是坏人。
京剧里的黑色的脸，不说假话。

nodes.say: 我叫英子。我的铃铛没有了……是骆驼的铃铛。
nodes.translate: I’m 英子. My bell is gone… a camel’s bell.
nodes.why: Homage to 林海音’s 《城南旧事》 (My Memories of Old Beijing, 1960): little 英子 grows up in the south of the city in the 1920s, when camel caravans still brought coal in.

nodes.say: 我的铃铛是黄色的，小小的，有声音。
nodes.simpler: 黄色的，小的铃铛，有声音。
nodes.translate: My bell is yellow, very small, and it rings when it moves.

words.explain: 一动就有声音的小东西。
很大的动物，背上有两个包。

nodes.say: 我的铃铛！谢谢你！你听，它的声音！
nodes.translate: My bell! Thank you! Listen: ding-dong, ding-dong.

nodes.say: 那个时候，骆驼来北京，都有这个声音。
nodes.translate: When the camels came to Beijing, they all made this sound.

words.explain: 一动就有声音的小东西。
很大的动物，背上有两个包。

nodes.translate: I am 孙悟空! I can transform!
nodes.why: Homage to 《西游记》 (Journey to the West): the Monkey King 孙悟空 knows seventy-two transformations. (猪八戒 eating the whole snack street is not built yet.)

nodes.say: 我变！红色的，可以吃，很好吃。我是什么？
nodes.translate: Transform! Red, you can eat it, very sweet. What am I?

nodes.say: 再变！很大，有四个门，可以坐人。我是什么？
nodes.translate: Again! Very big, four doors, goes along the road. What am I?
You know them all! I give up!

words.explain: 一个东西成了别的东西。

nodes.translate: I’m 哪吒! 哪吒 is the strongest!
nodes.why: 哪吒 is the boy-god of 《封神演义》 who rides wheels of fire — lately the hero of China’s biggest films. Which of the two is stronger is a playground argument everywhere.

nodes.speaker: wukong-xiaohai
nodes.translate: Wrong! 孙悟空 is the strongest!
You say — who’s stronger?

nodes.say: 我们都很厉害？好！我们是朋友！
nodes.translate: We’re both strong? All right — we’re friends!
Ha! See? I’m the strongest!
…Fine. We’ll have it out again tomorrow!

legend.zh: 过年的时候，人们在大门上画两个门神。门神看着门，不让坏东西进来。人们说，他们以前是两个很好的将军。
legend.en: At New Year people paint two door gods on their gates. They guard the door and keep bad things out. People say they were once two brave generals.

befriend.text: 我们的颜色都没了。你有红纸吗？
befriend.en: Bring red paper so they can be painted bright again.

idioms.meaning: to spoil something by adding what is not needed

story.zh: 几个人比画蛇，谁先画好，谁喝酒。一个人先画好了，他说：“我还能给蛇画脚！”他画脚的时候，别人画好了。别人说：“蛇没有脚！”酒是别人的了。
story.en: Several men raced to draw a snake; the first to finish would get the wine. One finished first and said, 'I can even add feet!' While he drew them, another finished and said, 'Snakes have no feet!' — and took the wine.
